item.text:
**7B.9 Assessment:** mixed, leaning negative. Marcos took several formal anti-patronage steps in 2024, especially on procurement, some appointments, and social-service delivery, but the broader political system still looked dynastic, transactional, and media-politicized, with family-network alliance signals and weak campaign-finance controls.

**Positive / mitigating evidence**
- [Speech of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. at the oath-taking and announcement of the new Department of Finance secretary and special assistant to the president for investment and economic affairs](https://pbbm.com.ph/speeches/speech-of-president-ferdinand-r-marcos-jr-at-the-oath-taking-and-announcement-of-the-new-department-of-finance-secretary-and-special-assistant-to-the-president-for-investment-and-economic-affairs/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-01-12 | Claim: Marcos framed Frederick Go and Ralph Recto as competence-based choices, which is direct evidence against purely nepotistic appointments. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.5
- [PBBM says Comelec has mandate to probe alleged signature-buying for PI](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217440) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-23 | Claim: Marcos said he would not meddle in Comelec’s probe of alleged signature-buying, which is evidence of procedural restraint rather than executive capture. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6
- [PBBM orders agencies to help COS, JO workers get permanent positions in government](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-agencies-to-help-cos-jo-workers-get-permanent-positions-in-government/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-25 | Claim: Instead of staffing through patronage, Marcos told agencies to help long-serving contract workers qualify for permanent posts through training and eligibility. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.5
- [Philippines: New Government Procurement Act Enters into Force](https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2024-10-03/philippines-new-government-procurement-act-enters-into-force/) | Library of Congress | 2024-10-03 | Claim: The new procurement law was framed around transparency, public monitoring, and accountability, which cuts against favoritism and transactional contracting. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.6
- [PBBM stands by suspension of 139 NFA officials](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-stands-by-suspension-of-139-nfa-officials/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-03-06 | Claim: Marcos backed suspensions over anomalous rice sales and procedural irregularities, which is evidence against shielding insiders from enforcement. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.7
- [PBBM issues EO No. 52, institutionalizing and expanding DSWD’s Pag-abot Program](https://mirror.pia.gov.ph/press-releases/2024/01/22/pbbm-issues-eo-no-52-institutionalizing-and-expanding-dswds-pag-abot-program-for-street-dwellers-other-poor-and-vulnerable-individuals) | PIA / PCO | 2024-01-22 | Claim: Pag-Abot was formalized with an inter-agency structure and monitoring, which is evidence of programmatic delivery rather than ad hoc clientelism. | QIDs: 7B.9
- [Philippine News Agency: eFOI and media-literacy / disinformation efforts](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | Claim: The administration expanded public access through eFOI and kept media-literacy/disinformation measures in place, which modestly supports access to public information. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.6

**Negative / concerning evidence**
- [Marcos, Romualdez parties forge political alliance](https://www.bworldonline.com/the-nation/2024/05/08/593686/marcos-romualdez-parties-forge-political-alliance/) | BusinessWorld Online | 2024-05-08 | Claim: The Marcos and Romualdez parties formed a formal alliance for the 2025 midterms, showing the family network remained fused to state power and electoral strategy. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.4, 7B.6
- [Philippines](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Claim: The report says TeleRadyo Serbisyo entered a joint venture with Prime Media associated with the Romualdez family, and that regulatory pressure over broadcasters persisted. That is indirect but real evidence of family-linked business access and politicized media regulation. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.4, 7B.6, 7B.7
- [Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: Freedom House says campaign-finance rules are weak, vote buying is widespread, and patronage/kinship still shape politics, which is strong background evidence for transactional politics. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.6, 7B.7
- [Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Claim: Red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted under Marcos, weakening the case that independent scrutiny and public information were cleanly protected. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.7, 7B.6
- [Marcos bans offshore gaming operators](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-marcos-orders-closure-offshore-100722060.html) | Reuters via Yahoo News | 2024-07-22 | Claim: The POGO ban is a clear anti-rent move, but it also shows the administration had to intervene against a sector entangled with criminal money and political leverage rather than a cleanly neutral marketplace. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.7
- [House panel flags possible collusion among rice importers after tariff cuts](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1239684) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-12-10 | Claim: A House panel flagged possible collusion in a major policy area, suggesting a regulatory domain that remained vulnerable to insider gains and capture. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.4, 7B.6

**Search gap**
- I did not find a solid 2024 source showing Marcos personally awarding pardons, jobs, contracts, or media access to named relatives or cronies.
- The negative case is mostly structural and indirect: dynastic alliance, family-linked media/business ties, weak campaign finance, and persistent media pressure, rather than a single smoking-gun nepotism incident.
